stories.headline: Small island states prepare for a likely 1.5°C climate overshoot
stories.summary: A Global Issues/IPS report highlights UNEP’s warning that the world is now expected to cross the 1.5°C warming threshold, with small island communities facing saltwater intrusion, coral reef loss, coastal flooding, and pressure on already thin adaptation resources.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a moment to pray beyond the headlines for neighbours whose homes, food, and water are becoming fragile. Creation care is not abstraction here; it is love of neighbour at planetary scale.

stories.headline: More than 30 Christians reported killed in Plateau State, Nigeria
stories.summary: Morning Star News reports that suspected Fulani herdsmen killed more than 30 Christians in Mangu County, Plateau state, over the past month, including attacks on Bin-Per, Kinat, Kop-Naanle, and Fungtim communities. Local leaders also reported burned homes, destroyed crops, and victims including women and children.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold Nigeria’s church before the Lord today. Their suffering calls us away from vague concern into intercession, advocacy, and solidarity with the body of Christ when one part suffers.

stories.headline: Pew: Most adults under 50 say they spend too much time on smartphones
stories.summary: Pew Research Center reports that 53% of U.S. adults say they spend too much time on their smartphones. The concern is especially strong among younger adults: 70% of adults ages 18–29 and 64% of those ages 30–49 say their phone use is excessive.
stories.pastoral_note: This is fertile ground for discipleship: people already feel the bondage of distraction. The church can offer not merely tech tips, but practices of attention, Sabbath, embodied presence, and prayer.

stories.headline: Notre Dame to convene leaders on AI, faith, and human flourishing
stories.summary: Notre Dame’s Institute for Ethics and the Common Good will host the 2026 DELTA Summit on AI, Faith, and Human Flourishing later this month, gathering leaders from industry, education, and pastoral ministry to consider formation, moral discernment, and faithful responses to AI.
stories.pastoral_note: The AI question is ultimately a formation question: what kind of people are we becoming? Pastors can help congregations move beyond fear or fascination into wisdom, creatureliness, and love.

stories.headline: HBR asks whether great leaders are truly great — or just lucky
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review’s Sept. 1 leadership podcast features historian Jared Diamond arguing that organizations often over-credit powerful figures while underestimating timing, circumstance, industry conditions, and plain luck. His “Hamlet test” asks whether another person could have achieved the same outcome.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a healthy corrective for ministry leadership. Faithful leaders should steward moments with courage, but resist the myth that fruitfulness is proof of personal greatness. Humility keeps leadership sane.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley remains a buyer’s market with benchmark prices down year over year
stories.summary: A Fraser Valley housing market update reports a July 2026 composite MLS HPI benchmark of $871,200, down 7.1% year over year, with single-family, townhouse, and apartment benchmarks also lower. The most recent full FVREB breakdown cited March 2026 buyer’s-market conditions and a sales-to-active-listings ratio of 10.9%.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing pressure continues to shape pastoral care in the Lower Mainland — anxiety for sellers, exhaustion for renters, and cautious hope for some buyers. Keep asking how affordability is discipling people’s choices, stress, and sense of rootedness.

stories.headline: Global South cooperation offers practical hope for food security
stories.summary: IPS reports on FAO-supported South-South and Triangular Cooperation, where countries share tested agricultural expertise, technologies, and field practices. Examples include China, Brazil, Türkiye, and Central Asian partnerships strengthening food security and farmer livelihoods.
stories.pastoral_note: Not all global stories are collapse. This is a quiet picture of common grace: neighbours learning from neighbours, practical wisdom shared, and vulnerable communities strengthened through partnership rather than dependency.

stories.headline: Pew’s 25-years-after-9/11 portrait reveals an evangelistic challenge of fear and neighbour-love
stories.summary: Pew reports that many Americans still view Muslims through the lens of 9/11, with 43% saying Muslims are less patriotic than other Americans and 42% saying Muslim Americans have a negative impact on the country. The report also notes Muslim Americans as a growing and politically visible part of the U.S. religious landscape.
stories.pastoral_note: For Christians, this is a test of witness. Evangelism cannot be detached from neighbour-love; the gospel is most credible when we refuse fear, honour image-bearers, and bear witness to Christ with humility and courage.
